   INTRODUCTION
   Holmes was engaged by Portland Public Schools (PPS) in 2023 to update the seismic assessment inormation or each school campus
   within the district to aid in planning o uture projects and bond unding. The assessment included 80 total sites and only buildings that
   have not been the target o an in progress retroit or a recently completed retroit. Unreinorced Masonry (URM ) buildings were broken
   out due to their relatively high risk in order to be prioritized, which includes 23 sites on the provided URM List and 6 potential additional
   sites. The data provided by Holmes includes seismic vulnerabilities, estimated construction costs, and incorporating district provided
   inormation such as Title 1 designated schools. This report provides a high-level inormation on each target building as well as a portolio-
   level summary.


   PROJECT OVERVIEW
   ASSESSMENT DESCRIPTION
   The ollowing steps were perormed or each school building:
   1. Review available existing building documentation.
   2. Develop a Building Year Plan based on available drawings and /or historic aerial views. Identiy unreinorced masonry (URM )
   construction on Plan and approximate square ootage o URM areas, where occurs.
   3. Develop a list o potential deiciencies. The deiciencies list is inormed by the ASCE 41 Tier 1 structural checklists or each building
   type, but are not entirely comprehensive o the Tier 1 methodology.
   4. Perorm a site walk to conirm building conigurations and identiy visible deiciencies and site characteristics.
   5. Compile inormation and develop an engineer’s rough order o magnitude (ROM) pricing. Pricing is summarized by URM-only retroit
   as well as the complete ROM retroit or all buildings on the campus.

   The assessments utilized FEMA Rapid Visual Screening, ASCE 41 Tier 1 checklists, and Holmes’ experience with similar building types as a
   guideline to identiy deiciencies. However, these assessments were not a ull ASCE 41 Tier 1 assessment and all deiciencies require
   urther analysis and veriication to ollow the ASCE 41 methodology. Identiication o non-structural deiciencies is outside the scope o
   this study, however non-structural deiciencies which may pose a lie-saety hazard (i.e. parapets, masonry chimneys, interior
   unreinorced masonry walls) were noted in our assessments. See diagram below or more inormation on typical levels o seismic
   assessments compared to the level o assessment completed or this project.

## Page 2

```
   We have assessed and compiled the results or all PPS schools, excluding the ollowing
      Schools currently under design through Modernizations & New Construction
      Schools with complete or near complete recent seismic upgrade
    Schools recently constructed. Individual buildings that comply with the ASCE 41 Chapter 3 design years or Benchmark Buildings
   are also omitted rom the assessment and retroit costs, and are noted as such in the summary.


   PRICING NOTES
   Pricing has been calculated using a ROM (rough order o magnitude) $/SF cost or each building part. The costs are an engineer’s
   estimate based on Holmes’ experience with similar projects and only intended or initial budgeting purposes. All costs should be veriied
   by an experience cost estimator. URM-Only pricing provided is intended to give an approximate cost estimate to perorm a localized
   URM-Only retroit. This price is accompanied by the approximate cost to retroit all buildings on the campus. The square ootage noted
   is an approximate boundary or each building part to be retroitted, and has been scaled o existing documentation available.



   The cost is relective o the ollowing:
    Estimates are based on representative cost estimates provided in the last year (+/-) rom schematic design retroit pricing o similar
   buildings and/or building parts and is a ROUGH order o magnitude price. Appropriate contingencies and escalation should be applied.
    URM-Only retroits are or seismic upgrades within the URM area indicated in the Building Year Plan. While the retroit will be
   considered partial (localized only) it is intended to mitigate URM deiciencies as well as align with the scope associated with a ull
   seismic upgrade or that building part. For example, in addition to bracing o URM walls in the URM-Area-Only, the cost would include
   items such as re-roo, secondary gravity support, and oundation strengthening that would otherwise be required as part o a complete
   seismic upgrade, to avoid remobilization and demolition in the URM area.


    Estimates include consideration o demolition and repair o architectural inishes as required to complete the structural work, per the
   representative cost estimates provided.
    Estimates include consideration or MEP and architectural upgrades required (per the representative cost estimates provided ) as
   part o the seismic upgrade, in order to mitigate remobilization in this area in the event o a uture complete seismic upgrade, though
   these items have not been assessed as part o this scope.

      Sot costs such as engineering, construction management, and relocation are excluded.

   INTRODUCTION
   Holmes was engaged by Portland Public Schools (PPS) in 2023 to update the seismic assessment inormation or each school campus
   within the district to aid in planning o uture projects and bond unding. The assessment included 80 total sites and only buildings that
   have not been the target o an in progress retroit or a recently completed retroit. Unreinorced Masonry (URM ) buildings were broken
   out due to their relatively high risk in order to be prioritized, which includes 23 sites on the provided URM List and 6 potential additional
   sites. The data provided by Holmes includes seismic vulnerabilities, estimated construction costs, and incorporating district provided
   inormation such as Title 1 designated schools. This report provides a high-level inormation on each target building as well as a portolio-
   level summary.


   PROJECT OVERVIEW
   ASSESSMENT DESCRIPTION
   The ollowing steps were perormed or each school building:
   1. Review available existing building documentation.
   2. Develop a Building Year Plan based on available drawings and /or historic aerial views. Identiy unreinorced masonry (URM )
   construction on Plan and approximate square ootage o URM areas, where occurs.
   3. Develop a list o potential deiciencies. The deiciencies list is inormed by the ASCE 41 Tier 1 structural checklists or each building
   type, but are not entirely comprehensive o the Tier 1 methodology.
   4. Perorm a site walk to conirm building conigurations and identiy visible deiciencies and site characteristics.
   5. Compile inormation and develop an engineer’s rough order o magnitude (ROM) pricing. Pricing is summarized by URM-only retroit
   as well as the complete ROM retroit or all buildings on the campus.

   The assessments utilized FEMA Rapid Visual Screening, ASCE 41 Tier 1 checklists, and Holmes’ experience with similar building types as a
   guideline to identiy deiciencies. However, these assessments were not a ull ASCE 41 Tier 1 assessment and all deiciencies require
   urther analysis and veriication to ollow the ASCE 41 methodology. Identiication o non-structural deiciencies is outside the scope o
   this study, however non-structural deiciencies which may pose a lie-saety hazard (i.e. parapets, masonry chimneys, interior
   unreinorced masonry walls) were noted in our assessments. See diagram below or more inormation on typical levels o seismic
   assessments compared to the level o assessment completed or this project.

   We have assessed and compiled the results or all PPS schools, excluding the ollowing
      Schools currently under design through Modernizations & New Construction
      Schools with complete or near complete recent seismic upgrade
    Schools recently constructed. Individual buildings that comply with the ASCE 41 Chapter 3 design years or Benchmark Buildings
   are also omitted rom the assessment and retroit costs, and are noted as such in the summary.


   PRICING NOTES
   Pricing has been calculated using a ROM (rough order o magnitude) $/SF cost or each building part. The costs are an engineer’s
   estimate based on Holmes’ experience with similar projects and only intended or initial budgeting purposes. All costs should be veriied
   by an experience cost estimator. URM-Only pricing provided is intended to give an approximate cost estimate to perorm a localized
   URM-Only retroit. This price is accompanied by the approximate cost to retroit all buildings on the campus. The square ootage noted
   is an approximate boundary or each building part to be retroitted, and has been scaled o existing documentation available.



   The cost is relective o the ollowing:
    Estimates are based on representative cost estimates provided in the last year (+/-) rom schematic design retroit pricing o similar
   buildings and/or building parts and is a ROUGH order o magnitude price. Appropriate contingencies and escalation should be applied.
    URM-Only retroits are or seismic upgrades within the URM area indicated in the Building Year Plan. While the retroit will be
   considered partial (localized only) it is intended to mitigate URM deiciencies as well as align with the scope associated with a ull
   seismic upgrade or that building part. For example, in addition to bracing o URM walls in the URM-Area-Only, the cost would include
   items such as re-roo, secondary gravity support, and oundation strengthening that would otherwise be required as part o a complete
   seismic upgrade, to avoid remobilization and demolition in the URM area.


    Estimates include consideration o demolition and repair o architectural inishes as required to complete the structural work, per the
   representative cost estimates provided.
    Estimates include consideration or MEP and architectural upgrades required (per the representative cost estimates provided ) as
   part o the seismic upgrade, in order to mitigate remobilization in this area in the event o a uture complete seismic upgrade, though
   these items have not been assessed as part o this scope.

      Sot costs such as engineering, construction management, and relocation are excluded.
